patch.summary:
Thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — Shopify documents a broader use-case set; OpenCart is narrower/specialist.

Comparison thesis: General-purpose vs specialist. Choose OpenCart only if your buying job matches “GPL open-source PHP cart — free download core; optional managed cloud cited ~$59–$99/mo by” rather than Shopify's shape. Choose Shopify only if your buying job matches “Hosted SaaS ecommerce platform with themes, checkout, channels, and POS — Basic from $39/m” rather than OpenCart's shape. Workflow advantage: OpenCart leans shared coverage; Shopify leans catalog-management, checkout-conversion. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — Shopify documents a broader use-case set; OpenCart is narrower/specialist.
- Positioning: OpenCart is GPL open-source PHP cart — free download core; optional managed cloud cited ~$59–$99/mo by secondary sources (confirm live). WooCommerce kee; Shopify is Hosted SaaS ecommerce platform with themes, checkout, channels, and POS — Basic from $39/mo ($29 annual), Grow $105 ($79 annual), Advanced $.
- Company-size focus: OpenCart (small-business, mid-market) vs Shopify (solo, micro, small-business).
- Workflow coverage skew: OpenCart-leaning — vs Shopify-leaning catalog-management, checkout-conversion, omnichannel-retail.
- Researched limits: OpenCart — Hosting, security, and extension TCO are on you even when the license is $0; Shopify — Subscription plus apps/themes and payment spreads raise TCO versus headline plan price.

Limitations — OpenCart: Hosting, security, and extension TCO are on you even when the license is $0; Managed cloud floors are not first-party confirmed here — confirm live before budgeting; Shopify: Subscription plus apps/themes and payment spreads raise TCO versus headline plan price; Third-party payment gateways incur additional transaction fees on lower tiers.

Poor-fit cases: OpenCart is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Hosting, security, and extension TCO are on you even when the license is $0 · Shopify is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Subscription plus apps/themes and payment spreads raise TCO versus headline plan price · Avoid OpenCart if you actually need Shopify's motion (Hosted SaaS ecommerce platform with themes, checkout, channels, and POS — Basic )

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
